scope: Selected references from Jones (JEP 2026) and top-five journal publications/advance access 2022-01-01 through 2026-09-16. Introductory/mechanism passages reviewed, not every page or proof. Braxton and Taska remains abstract-only.

new_candidates.title: A Framework for Economic Growth with Capital-Embodied Technical Change
new_candidates.authors: Jones, Benjamin F. and Liu, Xiaojie
new_candidates.review: Candidate for paragraph-by-paragraph integration; not added to the manuscript. Review: Published AER PDF, pp. 1448-1450 (PDF 1-3), especially equation (2). This is a targeted reading, not a full audit of every proof, estimate or subsequent version.
new_candidates.connection: Use when distinguishing improvements in AI efficiency from expansion in the set of automated tasks, and when explaining production bottlenecks.
new_candidates.limit: Their task-automation margin is absent from our fixed aggregate production structure. Their elasticity is not automatically our AI-labor elasticity.

new_candidates.title: Tasks, Automation, and the Rise in U.S. Wage Inequality
new_candidates.review: Candidate for paragraph-by-paragraph integration; not added to the manuscript. Review: NBER w28920, original June 2021 working-paper version, introduction pp. 1-3 (PDF 3-5). new_candidates.connection: Use to distinguish displacement of tasks from job loss and from movements in a representative wage.
new_candidates.limit: No autonomous AI research or representative-household growth result. Group wage losses cannot be identified with our aggregate wage path.

new_candidates.title: Automation and Rent Dissipation: Implications for Wages, Inequality, and Productivity
new_candidates.review: Candidate for paragraph-by-paragraph integration; not added to the manuscript. Review: Author version November 2025, introduction pp. 1-3 (PDF 3-5); publication checked: QJE 141(2), May 2026. This is a targeted reading, not a full audit of every proof, estimate or subsequent version.
new_candidates.connection: Use in limitations when discussing workers' economic position beyond their marginal-product wage.
new_candidates.limit: Worker rents above outside options are not the same as AI-developer monopoly profit. Our competitive labor market omits this mechanism.

new_candidates.title: Inefficient Automation
new_candidates.review: Candidate for paragraph-by-paragraph integration; not added to the manuscript. Review: Typeset advance-access PDF (2024), pp. 1-3; final issue citation is ReStud 92(1), 2025, pp. 69-96. This is a targeted reading, not a full audit of every proof, estimate or subsequent version.
new_candidates.connection: Use to qualify welfare interpretations of rapid RSI transitions and motivate labor-market and financial frictions as extensions.
new_candidates.limit: Our representative household and frictionless labor allocation do not produce their pecuniary externality or establish an optimal automation tax.

new_candidates.title: Induced Automation Innovation: Evidence from Firm-Level Patent Data
new_candidates.authors: Hémous, David and Olsen, Morten and Zanella, Carlo and Dechezleprêtre, Antoine
new_candidates.review: Candidate for paragraph-by-paragraph integration; not added to the manuscript. Review: Published JPE HTML, sections I-II, and August 2022 predecessor PDF pp. 2-4 (PDF 3-5). new_candidates.limit: Machinery patents are not autonomous AI research; the estimated wage elasticity does not identify our research productivity or RSI elasticity.

new_candidates.title: Automation and Polarization
new_candidates.review: Candidate for paragraph-by-paragraph integration; not added to the manuscript. Review: Published JPE PDF, pp. 1017-1019 (PDF 1-3). This is a targeted reading, not a full audit of every proof, estimate or subsequent version.
new_candidates.connection: Use to explain why one aggregate elasticity cannot describe every occupation or worker.
new_candidates.limit: Comparative advantage and endogenous task assignment are absent from our representative-worker model; their results are not RSI growth predictions.

new_candidates.title: Data-intensive Innovation and the State: Evidence from AI Firms in China
new_candidates.authors: Beraja, Martin and Yang, David Y and Yuchtman, Noam
new_candidates.review: Candidate for paragraph-by-paragraph integration; not added to the manuscript. Review: CEP Discussion Paper 1755 (2021), introduction pp. 1-2 (PDF 3-4); final ReStud metadata checked separately. This is a targeted reading, not a full audit of every proof, estimate or subsequent version.

new_candidates.title: AI-tocracy
new_candidates.authors: Beraja, Martin and Kao, Andrew and Yang, David Y and Yuchtman, Noam
new_candidates.review: Candidate for paragraph-by-paragraph integration; not added to the manuscript. Review: NBER w29466, introduction pp. 1-2 (PDF 3-4); QJE publication details independently checked. This is a targeted reading, not a full audit of every proof, estimate or subsequent version.
new_candidates.connection: Possible reference for a clearly separate discussion of political power beyond income shares.

new_candidates.title: Market Power and Innovation in the Intangible Economy
new_candidates.review: Candidate for paragraph-by-paragraph integration; not added to the manuscript. Review: Published AER PDF, pp. 199-201 (PDF 1-3). This is a targeted reading, not a full audit of every proof, estimate or subsequent version.

new_candidates.limit: The model has heterogeneous firms and creative destruction, not a single permanent AI monopolist. It does not justify monopoly as universally growth enhancing.

new_candidates.title: Robot Arithmetic: New Technology and Wages
new_candidates.review: Candidate for paragraph-by-paragraph integration; not added to the manuscript. Review: LSE author manuscript, pp. 2-3. new_candidates.review: Candidate for paragraph-by-paragraph integration; not added to the manuscript. Review: Published AEJ: Macroeconomics PDF, pp. 2-3.
